rec.name: Competitor Comparison Table Section
rec.status: Reference only (already exists on live LARQ PDP; ticket marked duplicate)

what.text: A feature comparison table section on the product page. A headline and short subline on the left ("Makes others look old – The last bottle you'll ever need.") sit beside a table. Rows are product benefits (improves water quality, inactivates bacteria*, keeps the bottle clean, mercury-free, BPA- and plastic-free, long-lasting >100k cycles, no replacement filters, long-lasting battery 1 month). Columns are the brand's own product (LARQ Bottles, highlighted with a tinted column and coral check marks) versus three generic competitor categories (ordinary bottles, bottles with filters, mercury-containing UV pens). Cells show a check, cross or dash.

why.text: Side-by-side comparison lets shoppers evaluate the product against alternatives without leaving the page, which reduces the urge to shop around. The brand column is visually highlighted and shows a check in every row, which frames the product as the only complete solution (contrast effect and anchoring). Comparing against generic categories rather than named brands communicates unique value while avoiding direct competitor claims. A footnote asterisk and "dash" partial-support states add credibility.

how.text: Build as a theme section with a heading and subline block plus a table of rows. Each row has a label, an optional small sub-label (e.g. '>100k cycles', '1 month') and a status per column (yes / no / partial). Highlight the brand column with a tinted background and accent-colored checks. Use neutral dark check and cross icons for competitor columns and a dash for partial. On mobile, keep the brand column sticky or collapse into a scrollable table. A chevron icon appears at the start of each row, possibly for an expandable explanation, but this is not confirmed.

items: Column headers (brand + up to 3 competitor categories)
Highlight color for brand column and check accent color

dependencies.text: No dependencies are stated. Likely only theme section/block settings; metafields would be needed only if the table content varies per product. Claims such as bacteria inactivation need legal/substantiation backing (see asterisk).
